title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
slides: Fractile raises $720M. But can it really challenge Nvidia?
Its chips aim to run AI models faster and cheaper.
Yet the secret sauce is a memory trick most ignore.
For buyers, this means more choice and falling prices.
Test Fractile's benchmarks before locking into Nvidia.
thread_text:
1. $720M Bet Against Nvidia

Fractile just raised $720 million to build chips that run AI models faster and cheaper. The question is whether a memory trick most people ignore can actually break Nvidia's grip.

2. The Memory Trick

Fractile's chips use a memory architecture that most chip designers overlook. It lets AI models run with less data movement, which cuts both cost and latency.

3. Buyers Get Leverage

If Fractile delivers, buyers get a real alternative to Nvidia. More competition means falling prices and more choice, especially for companies priced out of top-tier GPUs.

4. The Catch

Fractile hasn't published independent benchmarks yet. The $720 million is a bet on a memory design that remains unproven at scale against Nvidia's ecosystem.

5. Test Before You Commit

Ask Fractile for benchmark numbers on your own model before signing an Nvidia contract. If they can't provide them, you have your answer.

$720 million says Nvidia's grip can be broken with a memory trick most chip designers overlook.

Fractile's chips move less data, which cuts cost and latency when running AI models. 🧠

If it delivers, buyers get a real alternative and prices fall — especially for teams priced out of top-tier GPUs.

But no independent benchmarks exist yet, so the design is unproven at scale. ⚠️

Before you renew an Nvidia contract, ask Fractile for benchmark numbers on your own model. 📊

If they can't provide them, doesn't that tell you everything? 🤔
